patterns.short_summary: The system takes the interrogative turn: it poses questions — clarification prompts, structured fields, interview turns — and the user's answers, rather than a user-composed prompt, constitute the specification the system works from.
The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates.
Instead of describing what they want, the user supplies one or more instances of it, and the system generalizes or inverts those instances into the operative specification.

An artifact the user already possesses or has produced — a draft, a collection, a document, a physical or staged arrangement, their own prior judgments — is ingested and used as the input the generation is conditioned on.
A property of the system or of its output is bound to an ordered control the user sets to a value — a slider, a numbered keypress, a discrete set of levels, a spatial distance.
Instead of an open input box, the system attaches the same small, named menu of prepared prompts to every content unit it holds.
The user places elements on an open two-dimensional surface and the system reads their positions and relations as specification.
The user's freehand mark — a stroke, a scribble, an arrow, a drawn layout — is taken as input to generation, either alongside or in place of a written prompt.

The user states in language what they want to be true of the artifact, and the system performs the corresponding edit or retrieval.
